text.text_excerpt: Love this place, and the ferry ride over from the French Quarter makes it an adventure. Super cozy interior with a great authentic British Pub feel. If you like a proper cocktail, their drinks are pretty outstanding. They use locally sourced small batch soda syrups, so the Pimm's Cup was fantastic - made separately with ginger and cucumber bitters (see pictures). Their signature drink best sellers are the Pimm's Cup and Proper English G&T. Great. Old weather drinks include Hot Buttered Rums and an awesome sounding "King Cake Old Fashioned" with some of the aforementioned bitters/syrups - one pecan. I'll be back to try that one.

A good "local" in a very convenient location near the ferry. My friends and I go over with our bikes on the ferry every once and awhile and the place never fails to entertain us. I love the little British touches, such as the crisps and candy from England. They also put the bar towels out, which I haven't seen since I was a kid (my dad is from London).. The regulars are really cool and welcoming, but not in a creepy manner. There was one guy who who apparently wasn't a regular who was very drunk and bugging all the ladies, but apparently he was not from the neighborhood. Great beer selection, AWESOME fast service, and lots of dogs to pet.. If you're in town and looking for something a lit...

Walk in and you're immediately transported to the British Isles. Now that I've read about the owner being a native on Yelp it all makes sense, because I haven't been in an authentic *Britisth* pub since... I was in England. I was very pleasantly surprised by the vibe of this place. I mean, you look out the window and are like, what the fuck are those palm trees doing there... I mean shouldn't there be a misty moor or foggy cliff to go brood about off in the distance? So stay inside (though that patio is pretty sweet). You'll want to. They are a friendly bunch in there.
